_comment: Regression baseline for the repair suite (SyntheticRGBD --suite repair,
fixture challenge.ldr, seed 7), checked by check_regression.py.
Each sampled step is built one stud off in four directions, judged from
a diagonal, a front, a side and an overhead view, and the planner's
repair is worded under all four screen rotations (M2.4).
harmful_actions must stay 0: an action that does not exactly undo the
shift would make the build worse. Direction disagreements with the
independent image-space projection are guarded lower_is_better.
Rows worded 'none' sit within 8 degrees of a sector boundary; the
diagonal regression view puts every stud-axis move there by design.
Cross-step rows (M2.9, flag on only in this suite): for each sampled step
the earlier part with the most built parts resting on it is shifted,
turned, missing, and missing under parts seen in place (which must be
withheld as implausible). Each plan is replayed on the support graph;
any step a builder could not take is harmful. The fixture has no part
with more than six resting on it, so the over-budget case does not occur.
